ac_evidence.ac: SDP-controlled MCP/write tools are classified as read or write capable.
ac_evidence.evidence: internal/mcp/tools.go:14 and internal/mcp/tools.go:38 define the hardcoded tool capability policy; internal/mcp/contract/mapping.go:57 carries capability in mapping contracts.

ac_evidence.ac: Duplicate or ambiguous tool names fail validation.
ac_evidence.evidence: internal/mcp/contract/mapping.go:270 rejects normalized ambiguous names; internal/mcp/contract/mapping_test.go:192 covers ambiguous tool names.

ac_evidence.ac: Untrusted MCP resource or tool-description text cannot authorize a write call.
ac_evidence.evidence: internal/mcp/server.go:639 gates write handlers through trusted_authorization; .pi/extensions/sdp.ts:59 blocks write-capable adapter commands without trustedAuthorization.

ac_evidence.ac: Read-then-write chains require trusted authorization for the write step.
ac_evidence.evidence: internal/mcp/tools.go:132 validates read-then-write chains; internal/mcp/tools_test.go:1084 covers the rejected and allowed chain cases.

ac_evidence.ac: Tests use mock/sandbox traces and do not depend on arbitrary third-party MCP server behavior.
ac_evidence.evidence: internal/mcp/tools_test.go:694, internal/mcp/tools_test.go:764, internal/mcp/tools_test.go:1084 use mock executors and in-memory policy traces only.
local test run: go test ./internal/mcp/... && go vet ./internal/mcp/... && go run ./cmd/sdp manifest validate

existing_work_summary: Pre-existing MCP server and mapping contract exposed SDP tools and resources, but did not classify write capability or gate write-capable MCP calls on trusted authorization.
